topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture series, introducing the lecturer and setting out the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Etiology of cancer: intrinsic factors versus environmental exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer development, examining how endogenous biological processes, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures combine to drive cancer risk across populations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and Burkitt lymphoma pathogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how oncogenic infectious agents contribute to cancer development, focusing on the specific epidemiological and molecular mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how dietary toxins, radiation, and chemical compounds cause DNA mutations either directly or following xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, including the distinction between initiators and promoters, inflammation-driven tumor outgrowth, and tissue vulnerability at specific developmental stages.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the complementary genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to detect carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic risk.
